dataIdInfo.idAbs: These ESRI shape files are of National Park Service tract and boundary data that was created by the Land Resources Division. Tracts are numbered and created by Lands cartographic staff are associated to the Land Status Maps. This data should be used to display properties that NPS owns and properties that NPS may have some type of interest such as scenic easements or right of ways.
dataIdInfo.idPurp: This data is intended to keep a record of ownership information. Tracts can represent several types of interest like fee and scenic easement, and can be under several types of ownership like NPS owned, private, other federal, state or county. This data set provides accurate and reliable ownership data for park management and acquisition priorities.

Consts.useLimit: NPS Director's Order #25 states: "Land status maps will be prepared to identify the ownership of the lands within the authorized boundaries of the park unit. These maps, showing ownership and acreage, are the 'official record' of the acreage of Federal and non-federal lands within the park boundaries. While these maps are the official record of the lands and acreage within the unit's authorized boundaries, they are not of survey quality and not intended to be used for survey purposes." As such this data is intended for use as a tool for GIS analysis. It is in no way intended for engineering or legal purposes. The data accuracy is checked against best available sources which may be dated and vary by location. NPS assumes no liability for use of this data. The boundary polygons LRD creates represent the current legislated boundary of a given NPS unit. NPS does not necessarily have full fee ownership or hold another interest (easement, right of way, etc...) in all parcels contained within this boundary. Equivalently NPS may own or have an interest in parcels outside the legislated boundary of a given unit. In order to obtain complete information about current NPS interests both inside and outside the units legislated boundary, the tracts file created by LRD should be used in conjunction with this boundary file created by LRD. Map features from all sources have been adjusted to achieve a ‘best fit’ registration to the ownership parcels. While great care was taken in this process, maps from different sources rarely agree as to the precise location of geographic features. The relative positioning of map features to one another results from combining different map sources without field ‘ground truthing’. Smaller scale maps have a larger level of inaccuracy. It is assumed that the boundary and tract information meets National Map Accuracy Standards and should be considered no better than the listed sources. Santa Monica Mountains National Recreation Area is in a status of continual update, and as newer/better data becomes available, it will be included in the Santa Monica Mountains National Recreation Area tract and boundary dataset. Any person or entity that relies on this data, does so at their own risk.

report.measDesc: The Tract_id, and Alpha data fields are included in the original GIS data. The Date_Edit data field is added when the data is made available to WASO for inclusion in the national data set. All remaining tract attributes are updated from LRD's Master Land Console (MLC). By default the Status and Estate fields are included shape file dbf. All other MDL fields covered under the FOIA can be added to this GIS data upon request.
Polygon topology was created using ArcPro. The data is then exported to ESRI shape file format and reprojected from it's native coordinate system to NAD83 generic latitude and longitude, LL83.

Information contained in LRD's land ownership databases is updated daily however tract polygons are posted to the NPS Data Store only when there is a change in geometry. To ensure ownership polygons have up to date ownership attribution use of Lands online map services is recommended. TractsNet AGOL (https://nps.maps.arcgis.com/apps/webappviewer/index.html?id=e32ce01fad374b1bb9a020c40316ce57) is available to all NPS employees. A public version of TractsNet AGOL is also available (https://nps.maps.arcgis.com/apps/webappviewer/index.html?id=43bc9db4736140e88e661c67460936e6). Please contact the data originator with any suggested corrections and updates. LRD's boundary polygons represent the current legislated boundary of a given NPS unit. NPS does not necessarily have full fee ownership or hold another interest (easement, right of way, etc...) in all parcels contained within this boundary. Equivalently NPS may own or have an interest in parcels outside the legislated boundary of a given unit. In order to obtain complete information about current NPS interests both inside and outside the units legislated boundary, LRD's tracts files should also be downloaded and used in conjunction with LRD's boundary files. Only two tracts or less than 0.1 percent in this data were not found in the ownership database maintained by the Land Resources Program. NPS currently has no information about these tracts.
Horizontal accuracy for this data meets or exceed National Map Accurcay Standards for 1:24,000 scale data.

prcStep.stepDesc: April 7, 2020 Update. Modified tracts 126-66, 126,69, and 126-70 based on county parcel data. In 2020: Several change orders were created by Lands regional cartographer to reconcile SAMO GIS data with the ownership databases maintained by the Land Resources Division. These change orders were applied to Lands ownership databases by the Pacific West Region and to the GIS data by WASO. In 2019: The SAMO data was compared with Los Angeles city and county parcel data as well as Ventura County Parcel Data. The data was also compaired with data provided by SAMO GIS Specialists and modified as appropriate. When necessary boundaries were COGO from legal descriptions and adjusted as required. Topology was re-created and corrected using ArgGIS Pro. Data was validated against the information in ownership database maintained by the Land Resources Program and all outstanding change orders were applied. In 2015 Data was adjusted based on new survey data from BLM. In 2003: Data was digitize from Santa Monica Mountains NRA Land Status Map using AutoCad in CA State Plane, NAD83, feet. Clean Topology was developed and attributes were assigned in AutoCad Map using the Drawing Clean-up function at a tolerance level of 0.10 and Object Data links. Data was then reprojected and exported to an ArcInfo Interchange file (*.e00) in UTM, Zone 11, NAD27, meters. Attributes were retrieved from the Master Deeds List (MDL) and were linked during the creation process in AutoCad using MAP object data link. Attributes were verified by displaying the lines in both the database and the spatial coverage, but no formal tests were performed. All Lands boundary and ownership polygons are created, imported, edited, attributed, approved, and topology is developed both for the data according to the procedures described in the Land Acquisition Procedures Manual Chapter 5. The entire unit is created in a single geographically contiguous project. The tract and boundary data is then reprojected to North American Datum 1983 generic latitude & longitude and exported to an ArcView shape file format.
